text.p: Online service CompuServe Inc. and Cyber Promotions Inc., accused of deluging CompuServe subscribers with junk e-mail, reached an out-of-court settlement banning Cyber Promotions from sending unsolicited e-mail to subscribers, the companies announced Tuesday.
Columbus, Ohio-based CompuServe said the companies will ask a U.S. district judge in Ohio to approve the settlement of the online service's case against Philadelphia-based Cyber Promotions.
The order also would require Cyber Promotions to prohibit any of its customers from sending unsolicited e-mail to CompuServe subscribers, the world's No. 2 online service said.

Cyber Promotions -- whose e-mailed advertisements have incurred the wrath of other Internet access providers -- will pay CompuServe $65,000 for legal fees incurred in obtaining the order, the online service said.
Cyber Promotions also will have to pay the online service undisclosed damages if it violates the order, CompuServe said.
CompuServe said it would allow Cyber Promotions to buy advertising on the online service and that such purchases could be used to offset legal fees.

CompuServe won a temporary restraining order against Cyber Promotions in October to prevent the bulk e-mailer from making its unsolicited e-mail messages look like they were being sent from a CompuServe computer.
The final consent order makes this provision permanent, CompuServe said.
In February, the restraining order was expanded to a preliminary injunction that also prohibited Cyber Promotions from sending subscribers unsolicited e-mail.

"Initially, CompuServe wanted a blanket block of all mail sent by Cyber Promotions to CompuServe members," Cyber Promotions President Sanford Wallace. "Through this settlement CompuServe agreed to not block and to allow Cyber Promotions to send mail to subscribers who wish to receive it."

The president of CompuServe's Interactive Services unit, Denny Matteucci, said in a statement, "CompuServe has taken an industry leadership position in combating unsolicited e-mail on behalf of all online/Internet users.

"This precedent-setting victory will be cited in future cases by other access providers in the ongoing industry war on unsolicited e-mail. Most online subscribers do not want unsolicited e-mail and we're responding to those members' concerns to preserve both their time and money."
